column11: derived: Merck generated $39,599mm of free cash flow on $189,294mm of revenue over 2023, 2024 and 2025, a 20.92% margin, against the 29.5% its cost of sales, SG&A and R&D leave. Solved so the modelled book reproduces that margin rather than assumed from one line's cost structure: the alliance rows carry no cost of sales and Animal Health carries its own, so a ratio taken off a single product does not reconcile the company. Restated before interest: MRK paid $3,700mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.95% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 12.10% to 10.14%. Restated at replacement capex: MRK spent $11,347mm on plant over 2023 to 2025 against $6,977mm of plant depreciation, 2.31% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 10.14% to 7.48%. Restated without one-off cash: MRK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried $8,300mm of deal payments in operating cash flow, capital allocation whose assets the book values separately; $572mm of legal settlements; $1,200mm of US transition tax (2025 instalment 1,200mm). column11: one stated segment count over the parent pool. CG Oncology FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-079498, filed 2026-02-27, Item 1 Business, opened and read 2026-11-14): 'Based on internal research derived from NIH SEER database, secondary claims data analytics and management assumptions, the high-risk BCG-naive NMIBC segment may represent up to 25,000 addressable patients.' That is KEYNOTE-676 Cohort B's population exactly. 25,000 / 84,530 = 0.295753. The same filing gives 25,000 for the high-risk BCG-unresponsive segment, 50,000 for high-risk BCG-exposed, 50,000 for intermediate-risk and 150,000 for high-risk and intermediate-risk together, so the two book seeds that quote it differently (jnj_inlexzo.csv as unresponsive, pfe_pf_06801591.csv as naive) are both right. Cross-check on the ratio: about 75% of incident bladder cancers are non-muscle-invasive (Nielsen ME et al., Cancer 2014;120(1):86-95, doi 10.1002/cncr.28397) and high-risk disease is roughly 40% of those, which gives about 25,400
column12: A FLOOR, AND THE REFUSAL IS WRITTEN HERE. KEYNOTE-676 Cohort A, high-risk NMIBC persistent or recurrent after one adequate BCG induction course, is NOT in this figure. CG Oncology's filing counts BCG-exposed high-risk disease at up to 50,000 and BCG-unresponsive at up to 25,000, but publishes no count for the exposed band that is not yet unresponsive, which is what Cohort A enrols; no other free US source for it was found (SEER Cancer Stat Facts, the CG Oncology, Johnson & Johnson and Pfizer 10-Ks, and the AUA/ASCO/SUO NMIBC guideline were searched on 2026-11-14). Taking the whole 50,000 would double-count the unresponsive patients the label already reaches. The pool is therefore Cohort B only and the layer is a floor

column11: two published shares, both already in the book, multiplied against KEYNOTE-992's own criteria. (1) 0.25 muscle-invasive at diagnosis: Nielsen ME, Smith AB, Meyer AM, Kuo TM, Tyree S, Kim WY, Milowsky MI, Pruthi RS, Millikan RC, 'Trends in stage-specific incidence rates for urothelial carcinoma of the bladder in the United States: 1988 to 2006', Cancer 2014;120(1):86-95 (doi 10.1002/cncr.28397, PMID 24122346), on US SEER cases, 'approximately 75% of incident cases found to be superficial to the muscularis propria', the share jnj_inlexzo.csv takes for this descriptor. (2) 0.102 treated with trimodal bladder-sparing therapy: Davies-Teye BB, Siddiqui MM, Zhang X et al., 'Treatment Patterns and Radical Cystectomy Outcomes in Patients Diagnosed With Urothelial Nonmetastatic Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer in the United States', Cancer Med 2025;14(4):e70644 (doi 10.1002/cam4.70644, PMC11822655, open access, read 2026-11-14), National Cancer Database, 83,259 cT2-cT4a cM0 urothelial MIBC patients diagnosed 2004 to 2017, of whom 'RC, trimodal treatment, and transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) plus chemotherapy were 34,715 (41.7%), 7,372 (8.9%), and 6,171 (7.4%), respectively', with trimodal use rising 'from 7.9% to 10.2%' across the period; the 10.2% endpoint is the figure jnj_inlexzo.csv reads from the same paper. 0.25 x 0.102 = 0.0255, about 2,156 patients a year
column12: KEYNOTE-992 restricts further to N0M0 where the NCDB cohort is any cN, and excludes diffuse CIS and poor bladder function, so the trial's own population is a little narrower than this pool. Pushing the other way, trimodal use was still rising at the end of the NCDB window and a positive BI-EFS result is itself an argument for more bladder preservation, so 10.2% is a share this readout would move

column11: ANCHOR, measured: 262 of 426 US patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who started concurrent chemoradiation, 61.5%, went on to consolidation durvalumab (Arunachalam A et al., PLoS One 2024;19(11):e0314156, PMC11588217, US Oncology Network, starts 2017 to 2019); death (28.3%) and progression (22.2%) were the main reasons the rest did not. It is the book's one measured US capture for an anti-PD-(L)1 added to a definitive chemoradiation regimen given with curative intent, and azn_oleclumab.csv already carries it. MULTIPLE 1.0, taken whole and said so: the eligible pool above is already defined as the patients who receive trimodal therapy, pembrolizumab would be given concurrently with the chemoradiation they are having anyway rather than as a separate decision, and no checkpoint inhibitor is approved in this slot, so the ceiling is the share of the pool fit enough to complete the regimen, which is what 61.5% measures
column12: a judgement on the multiple, not on the anchor. The case for lower: KEYTRUDA's own perioperative MIBC indication with enfortumab vedotin, added to the label in 2026, pulls the fitter MIBC patients towards cystectomy and away from this pool altogether. The case for higher: that same indication is Merck's own detailing of MIBC, which makes the sales call easier, not harder
